draft.title: Balance and stability
card: Stability is how hard it is to knock a body off balance. A body is balanced when it can hold a position without toppling.
Base of support
the area between the points that touch the ground, such as the feet. A wider base makes a body more stable.
Centre of gravity
the point where the body's weight acts as if it were all in one place. A lower centre of gravity makes a body more stable.
Line of gravity
an imaginary line running straight down from the centre of gravity. Stability is greater when this line falls near the middle of the base, and it is lost if the line moves outside the base.
draft.remember: More stable: wider base, lower centre of gravity, line of gravity over the base.

a.q: Which change would make a netball player more stable while she waits for a defender to push past her?
opts: Bending her knees and spreading her feet wider
Standing tall with her feet close together
Rising onto her toes with her feet close together
Leaning to one side with her feet close together
a.why: Bending the knees lowers her centre of gravity and spreading the feet widens her base, so both make her more stable. Rising onto her toes is tempting because it feels ready to move, but it raises her centre of gravity and narrows her base.
a.clue: Think about both the width of her base and the height of her centre of gravity.

b.q: Jai stands on one leg and leans his upper body far to the right, so his line of gravity falls outside his foot. What is most likely to happen?
opts: He loses balance, because the line is outside his base
He stays balanced, because his centre of gravity is low
He stays balanced, because leaning adds weight to his base
He loses balance, because his base is too wide
b.why: Stability is lost when the line of gravity falls outside the base of support, so Jai is likely to topple towards the right. His centre of gravity being low would help, but it cannot make up for a line of gravity that has left a narrow base.
b.clue: Where does the line of gravity fall compared with his foot?

a.best: Bending her knees and spreading her feet wider

b.best: He loses balance, because the line is outside his base

problems.detail: Why (b) says 'His centre of gravity being low would help', as if Jai's centre of gravity were low. The stem never says this, and standing upright on one leg does not suggest a low centre of gravity. It should say something like 'Even a low centre of gravity cannot make up for...'.
